subject_entity.notes: Origen's systematic theological work composed in Alexandria c. 220–230; the first attempt at a comprehensive Christian theology; four books covering God and the Trinity, the created world, free will, and Scripture; source for the doctrines of eternal generation of the Son, pre-existence of souls, universal restoration (apokatastasis), and allegorical exegesis; preserved mostly through Rufinus's sanitized Latin translation and fragments in Justinian's condemnation.

object_entity.proposition_label: The rule of faith is received from the apostles
object_entity.description: Christians hold to a received standard of teaching traced to the apostles and guarded by their successors.

evidence.notes: Origen explicitly recites the apostolic rule of faith in the Preface.

passage.excerpt: The following are the particular points which are clearly delivered in the teaching of the apostles: First, that there is one God who created and arranged all things; second, that Jesus Christ was begotten of the Father before all creatures, and after he had ministered to the Father in the creation of all things, in the last times emptied himself and was made man; third, that the Holy Spirit was associated in honour and dignity with the Father and the Son.
passage.notes: Origen's rule of faith in the Preface to De Principiis; trinitarian formula and apostolic tradition
